inventory.name: navigator.ml — the ML entry point the page heads 'navigator.ml → ML' (partial interface NavigatorML's readonly attribute ml)
MLContext — the device-side context the page heads 'MLContext', created by navigator.ml.createContext()
MLGraphBuilder — the graph construction API the page heads 'MLGraphBuilder', bound to an MLContext
MLGraph — the opaque compiled graph the page heads 'MLGraph', returned by builder.build()
navigator.ml.createContext(options?) — device preference ('cpu'/'gpu'/'npu') and power preference ('high-performance'/'low-power'/'default'); resolves to MLContext
MLContext.compute(graph, inputs, outputs) — page-documented run-inference call taking ArrayBufferView-keyed objects and returning Promise<MLComputeResult>
MLContext.createTensor(descriptor, writable?, readable?) — page-documented allocation of a device-side MLTensor for zero-copy sharing with WebGPU
MLContext.dispatch(graph, inputs, outputs) — page-documented fire-and-forget variant for MLTensor-backed buffers, with results staying device-side until readTensor()
new MLGraphBuilder(context) — the constructor that binds a builder to a context
MLGraphBuilder.input(name, descriptor) — declares an input operand from { dataType, dimensions }
MLGraphBuilder.constant(descriptor, data) — embeds a constant such as model weights into the graph at build time

MLGraphBuilder operator set the page enumerates (add, mul, matMul, conv2d, relu, sigmoid, softmax, transpose, reshape, gather, layerNormalization, gru, lstm, 'and ~70 more') — each returns an MLOperand
MLGraphBuilder.build(outputs) — compiles the graph from a name-to-MLOperand map and resolves to MLGraph

notes: Page edit 2026-10-06: ten ids were added to existing headings only (at-a-glance, why-it-exists, shape-of-the-api, navigator-ml, mlcontext, mlgraphbuilder, mlgraph, example-add-two-matrices, example-softmax-classifier, browser-support); no prose, example block, section or styling was added, reworded or restructured, and every added id is referenced by a selector below. The page already carried two <pre><code> blocks, so none was added: syntax points at the section carrying the page's declaration grammar (the call-form tables under 'shape of the API' — navigator.ml.createContext(options?), the MLContext and MLGraphBuilder member rows, and the { dataType, dimensions } option descriptors), while examples points at the two runnable <pre><code> examples. SOURCE DISAGREEMENTS (every cited source re-fetched 2026-10-06; both sides stated, neither adjudicated): (1) compute() — the page documents MLContext.compute(graph, inputs, outputs) returning Promise<MLComputeResult> and both of its examples call context.compute(...), while the spec URL the page links (https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webnn, fetched 2026-10-06, self-described as an Editor's Draft dated 10 September 2026) declares no compute() member on MLContext at all, exposing instead dispatch(MLGraph, MLNamedTensors, MLNamedTensors) plus createTensor/readTensor/writeTensor/exportToGPU. (2) createTensor signature — the page documents createTensor(descriptor, writable?, readable?), while that fetched spec declares Promise<MLTensor> createTensor(MLTensorDescriptor descriptor) with readable and writable as boolean members of MLTensorDescriptor : MLOperandDescriptor. (3) descriptor field name — the page's input() row and both examples use { dataType, dimensions }, while the fetched spec's MLOperandDescriptor declares dataType plus shape. (4) operator spelling — the page's operator list and softmax example write matMul, while the fetched spec IDL contains no matMul and spells it matmul (0 occurrences of 'matMul' in the fetched IDL). (5) operator count — the page presents 13 named operators 'and ~70 more' as of the January 2026 Candidate Recommendation snapshot, while the fetched spec's MLGraphBuilder block declares 91 MLOperand-returning operator methods (95 including input/constant, constant() having three overloads). (6) spec maturity — the page's at-a-glance row calls the linked spec a 'Candidate Recommendation', while the fetched document presents itself as 'Editor's Draft, 10 September 2026' and the ChromeStatus record the page links (fetched 2026-10-06, last updated 2026-04-08) gives spec maturity short_text 'Working draft' ('Specification currently under development in a Working Group'). (7) Chrome 147 origin trial and flag — the page's at-a-glance and browser-support rows say 'Origin trial in 147' with flag chrome://flags/#web-machine-learning-neural-network, while the linked ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06, last updated 2026-04-08) reports chrome status 'Proposed', origintrial false, flag false, is_released false and milestone_str 'Proposed'; only the flag_name 'web-machine-learning-neural-network' matches the page. (8) explainer section references — the page cites 'the WebNN explainer §1 ("Background")' and 'explainer §3–§6', while the explainer fetched 2026-10-06 (main branch) has no section titled 'Background' and no numbered sections; its headings are 'What's all this then?', Goals, Non-goals, Target hardware, Getting started, Key scenarios, Detailed design discussion, Considered alternatives, References & acknowledgements. (9) Edge code sharing — the page says Edge ships WebNN 'from the same code' as Chrome, while the linked ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) states only that the Chromium implementation is a Google/Intel/Microsoft collaboration and that Edge will launch WebNN at the same time as Chrome, with no statement about shared code. CORROBORATED CLAIMS: Firefox 'Positive' matches the mozilla/standards-positions issue #1215 label 'position: positive' and the ChromeStatus ff view (both fetched 2026-10-06); Safari 'No signal (Apple active in WG)' matches the ChromeStatus safari view note (fetched 2026-10-06); 'over 100 spec changes since April 2024' matches the fetched spec's status section ('Between Candidate Recommendation Snapshot 11 April 2024 and 22 January 2026 ... over 100 significant changes'); the DirectML / ML Compute / NPU mapping in 'why it exists' matches the fetched explainer's Target hardware section. The ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) marks privacy and security review 'Pending'; this page does not reproduce those fields, which is why securityPrivacy is not-applicable for every item. SCOPE OF THE INVENTORY: it covers the page's four core interfaces and the members its tables document. MLTensor, MLOperand and MLComputeResult are named by the page only as value/return types inside those rows ('Each returns an MLOperand', 'Promise<MLComputeResult>', the MLTensor buffer-sharing warning), so they are not separate inventory items, and this page carries no IDL block for the schema's outOfScope field to describe. Compatibility is feature-level: the page has one browser-support table and no per-member compatibility data, so every item cites it. UNEXERCISED EXAMPLE COVERAGE: createTensor and dispatch are documented by the page's table rows only — neither <pre><code> example uses them (both examples cover the operand/ArrayBufferView path), so their examples dimension points at the closest existing workflow example, which is weaker coverage than the rest of the inventory. DIVERGENCE NOT PINNED: per the B1 brief the implementer owns divergence disclosure and pinning, so nothing above was adjudicated or pinned. The sibling page v147/web-neural-network-api-webnn was not read or edited, so no sibling-vs-page contradiction was searched for.
